title: Mailbox envelope header
description: The metadata block at the top of one envelope file. The body is everything after the header and is stored as literal bytes, never re-encoded - which is why it is not a field here. body_sha256 is what makes 'verbatim' checkable instead of merely promised: an envelope edited after the fact fails verification rather than passing quietly.

run_id.description: The dispatch run this envelope belongs to, matching the run the dispatch state was opened under.

seq.description: Position in the run's envelope order. Assigned by the writer, never reused: the mailbox refuses to write over an existing envelope, so a repeated seq is a failed write rather than a silent overwrite.

kind.description: failure is written by the orchestrator ABOUT a worker that produced no report. It is not a worker saying it failed - that would be a report. The distinction is the whole of D6: silence has to become a record, and a record nobody wrote is not one.

from.description: Who the content is from, logically. A worker may be 'from' an envelope it did not write.

persisted_by.description: Who actually wrote the file. Never a worker: a worker constrained enough to be trusted holds no write tool, so it CANNOT write its own envelope, and an envelope claiming otherwise describes a worker with more capability than its role grants. D9 is enforced by this pattern rather than asked for in prose.

failure_mode.description: Required on a failure envelope: what went wrong, in one token, so a reader can tell a killed worker from one that ran out of turns. Absent on every other kind.
